title: Deferred Rejoin and Healing Protocol for Node Upgrade Safety
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Upgrades and node drains in dedicated pools can cause transient traffic-induced regressions when a host rejoins too early. Rejoins that accept traffic before KV cache warmup, lease reconciliation, and token quota reissuance increase tail latency and cause SLO blips.

Goal: Implement a deferred rejoin protocol and accompanying healing checks that prevent nodes from advertising capacity until they pass deterministic sanity gates. This reduces SLO perturbation during rolling upgrades, hotfix deploys, and autoscaler-triggered scaling events while preserving overall throughput and minimizing wasted capacity.

Proposal summary:
1) Deferred rejoin window: after an orchestrated drain/upgrade cycle, a node marks itself "pending-rejoin" and waits for a configurable preflight (default 90s) before it will accept external routing.
2) Deterministic preflight checks: KV cache occupancy threshold, latest-model-version alignment, active lease reconciliation with central allocator, quota token reissuance success, and a small tail-latency microbenchmark run (in-process generation to measure 95th percentile).
3) Healing protocol: if preflight fails, node enters an automated healing loop that attempts state repair in stages (local kv-warmup, delta sync from peers, selective kube cordon + restart). If healing repeatedly fails, node triggers a controlled eviction/retire flow and surfaces an incident with automatic capacity redistribution.
4) Tokenized rejoin lease: nodes obtain a short-lived 'rejoin lease' from the conductor which controls how much traffic they can accept while gradually ramping to full capacity (slotized increments over N seconds).
5) Observability and runbook: expose per-node preflight status, rejoin-lease progress, and healing attempts in Console; add an operator playbook for manual intervention and fast rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Nodes must not be routed traffic until they pass KV occupancy >= 70% OR complete a verified delta sync
A rejoin-lease mechanism exists that caps incoming concurrency and ramps to full capacity in at most 180s
Automated healing attempts are recorded and trigger a controlled eviction after 3 failed attempts
Synthetic canary workload shows <=5% change in 95th percentile latency during a 50-node rolling upgrade compared to baseline
Metrics and traces for preflight checks are visible in Console and Grafana dashboards
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind fleet-ops.allow_deferred_rejoin; unit tests and integration harness (local k8s + mock allocator)
Phase 1: Canary 5% of non-critical dedicated pools with rejoin lease capped at 20% concurrency
Phase 2: Expand to 50% with KV prefetch enabled and automated healing enabled
Phase 3: Full rollout to all dedicated pools after 2 weeks of stable metrics and no SLO regressions
Rollback: flip flag off and gracefully remove rejoin lease; triggers immediate draining for any node failing preflight
risks: Over-long deferred windows waste capacity under high load; mitigated via adaptive window tuned by recent fleet utilization
False positives in preflight (e.g., temporary network hiccup) may cause unnecessary evictions — add retry/backoff and soft-fail thresholds
Complexity in conductor lease code could create regressions; we'll run a targeted property test suite and peer review
Interplay with autoscaler: rejoin-lease ramping and autoscaler scaling decisions must be coordinated to avoid oscillation
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease issuance and expiry, hash-based quota reconciliation, and preflight condition evaluation
Integration tests in staging with synthetic KV warmup delays and controlled failure injection
Load test: rolling upgrades under 80% fleet utilization to measure latency and throughput impact
Chaos test: random network partitions and pod restarts to validate healing and eviction thresholds
